title: 2020 HMMT February Guts Problem 9
statement: Let \(P(x)\) be the monic polynomial with rational coefficients of minimal degree such that \(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\), \(\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}, \frac{1}{\sqrt{4}}, \ldots, \frac{1}{\sqrt{1000}}\) are roots of \(P\). What is the sum of the coefficients of \(P\) ?

solutions.text:
For irrational \(\frac{1}{\sqrt{r}},-\frac{1}{\sqrt{r}}\) must also be a root of \(P\). Therefore

\[P(x)=\frac{\left(x^{2}-\frac{1}{2}\right)\left(x^{2}-\frac{1}{3}\right) \cdots\left(x^{2}-\frac{1}{1000}\right)}{\left(x+\frac{1}{2}\right)\left(x+\frac{1}{3}\right) \cdots\left(x+\frac{1}{31}\right)}\]

We get the sum of the coefficients of \(P\) by setting \(x=1\), so we use telescoping to get

\[P(1)=\frac{\frac{1}{2} \cdot \frac{2}{3} \cdots \frac{999}{1000}}{\frac{3}{2} \cdot \frac{4}{3} \cdots \frac{32}{31}}=\frac{1}{16000}\]
